title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Bowing And Prostration With The Universe General Result

questions.question: What does the person remember before bowing in this passage?
questions.answer: He remembers Allah’s greatness and power over all things.

questions.question: How are the sleeping plants, animals, suns, and stars described?
questions.answer: They are described like obedient workers and servants under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What does the person say as he bows?
questions.answer: He says that Allah is the Greatest.

questions.question: What big idea does the passage connect to prostration in the world?
questions.answer: It connects prostration to all creation obeying Allah in life, death, and renewal.

questions.question: When creatures finish their duties and pass away, what are they compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to a well-ordered army or obedient soldiers being dismissed.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to creatures after they are sent away through death?
questions.answer: They are brought back again, fully or partly, especially in spring, and return to service.

questions.question: What season is given as an example of creatures coming back to life?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: How does a human being act when following the example of creation?
questions.answer: He says Allah is the Greatest and goes down in prostration with humility.

questions.question: What feelings should a person have in prostration according to the passage?
questions.answer: He should feel wonder, love, humility, and a humble lowering of himself before Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say this prostration becomes for the person?
questions.answer: It becomes a kind of spiritual rising and closeness.

questions.question: How is the ‘Isha prayer described at the end of the first paragraph?
questions.answer: It is described as beautiful, joyful, wise, fitting, and very important.

questions.question: Why are the five daily prayers set at certain times, according to the last paragraph?
questions.answer: Because those times point to great changes, show Allah’s actions in the world, and remind people of His blessings.

questions.question: Which prayer is being explained in the target passage?
questions.answer: The night prayer, or ‘Isha prayer.

questions.question: What does saying “Allah is the Greatest” show before bowing?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah is higher and greater than everything in creation.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention plants, animals, suns, and stars together?
questions.answer: To show that all kinds of creation are under Allah’s rule.

questions.question: What command of Allah is mentioned to show His power to create?
questions.answer: His command that brings things into being right away.

questions.question: What happens every year and every century to many created things in the passage?
questions.answer: They complete their work, pass away, and are sent on by Allah’s command.

questions.question: Why is death described in an orderly way here?
questions.answer: To show that even death happens under Allah’s wisdom and control, not by chaos.

questions.question: What happens after this sending away when Allah gives life again?
questions.answer: Creation rises again and becomes ready to serve.

questions.question: What lesson should a person learn from creatures that die and are brought back?
questions.answer: He should learn to obey Allah humbly and worship Him.

questions.question: What is special about human prostration in this passage?
questions.answer: It is done with love, amazement, humility, and awareness of Allah’s beauty and mercy.

questions.question: What does “a sort of Ascension” mean here in simple words?
questions.answer: It means a spiritual lifting up and nearness to Allah through worship.

questions.question: How does the passage want the reader to feel about praying ‘Isha?
questions.answer: It wants the reader to see it as good, meaningful, uplifting, and worth doing.

questions.question: What three reasons are given for prayer times being chosen as they are?
questions.answer: They match major changes in creation, point to Allah’s lordly acts, and remind people of His gifts.

questions.question: What part of the prayer is mentioned first in this passage: bowing or prostration?
questions.answer: Bowing is mentioned first.

questions.question: What thought leads the worshipper to bow?
questions.answer: Thinking about Allah’s greatness and the obedience of creation.

questions.question: In the passage, what job-like role do stars and other created things have?
questions.answer: They are pictured as serving Allah in the world.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the way creation responds to Allah’s command?
questions.answer: Creation responds with full obedience.

questions.question: How is the passing away of creatures connected to prostration?
questions.answer: Their passing away is pictured like a prostration of obedience before Allah.

questions.question: What comparison is used for creatures when they leave their duties?
questions.answer: They are compared to disciplined troops leaving their posts.

questions.question: After creatures are brought to life again, what do they do?
questions.answer: They stand up again and prepare to serve their Lord.

questions.question: How should a person join this pattern of creation?
questions.answer: By worshipping Allah and making sajdah with humility.

questions.question: Which qualities of Allah are especially noticed when the person prostrates?
questions.answer: Allah’s mercy, beauty, perfection, and compassion.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about a human being’s size and place before Allah?
questions.answer: A human being is small, but he can honor Allah through humble worship.

questions.question: Why is the ‘Isha prayer called reasonable and appropriate?
questions.answer: Because it matches the signs of change, obedience, death, and renewal seen in creation.

questions.question: What is the main message of the final sentence of the target passage?
questions.answer: The set times of prayer are full of wisdom and are a rightful duty because they match Allah’s great signs and blessings.

questions.question: What does the worshipper think about Allah before saying “Allah is the Greatest” and bowing?
questions.answer: He thinks about Allah’s majestic greatness.

questions.question: What examples from creation are given to show Allah’s control at night?
questions.answer: Sleeping living things and the hidden heavenly bodies are mentioned.

questions.question: Why are created things described as soldiers and servants?
questions.answer: To show that they follow Allah’s orders faithfully.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does all creation do when its time of duty ends?
questions.answer: It submits to Allah and passes away in an ordered way.

questions.question: What does this teach us about death?
questions.answer: Death is part of Allah’s plan and happens under His command.

questions.question: What example shows that Allah brings things back after they have faded away?
questions.answer: The return of life in spring.

questions.question: How is spring described in meaning, even if not in those exact words?
questions.answer: It is like a wake-up call that brings life back.

questions.question: What should a person do after thinking about how creation obeys Allah?
questions.answer: He should fall in prostration before Allah.

questions.question: What kind of attitude should fill the heart in sujood?
questions.answer: Deep respect, love, amazement, and humility.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by calling this a kind of Ascension?
questions.answer: It means worship raises the person spiritually toward Allah.

questions.question: What judgment does the passage make about the ‘Isha prayer?
questions.answer: It says it is a noble, pleasant, and serious act of worship.

questions.question: Why is it wise for the daily prayers to happen at fixed times?
questions.answer: Because each time matches great changes in the world and reminds us of Allah’s blessings.

questions.question: What word best describes the main focus of the first part of the passage: Allah’s greatness, people’s wealth, or travel?
questions.answer: Allah’s greatness.

questions.question: What makes the worshipper bow in this passage?
questions.answer: Reflecting on Allah’s power and the obedience of creation.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give of the world and its creatures?
questions.answer: It gives a picture of a world where everything serves Allah by His command.

questions.question: What happens to creatures over time, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They finish their tasks, pass away, and are replaced or revived by Allah’s will.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare creatures to an army?
questions.answer: To show discipline, order, and obedience.

questions.question: What happens when Allah gives the order for life again?
questions.answer: Creatures rise and get ready again for service.

questions.question: How does this help explain human worship?
questions.answer: It shows that people too should obey Allah and worship Him humbly.

questions.question: What does the person say when he goes into prostration?
questions.answer: He says that Allah is the Greatest.

questions.question: Name two feelings the passage connects with prostration.
questions.answer: Wonder and humility.

questions.question: What higher result comes from this worship, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It becomes a means of spiritual nearness and rising.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the value of praying ‘Isha?
questions.answer: It describes it as lovely, uplifting, fitting, and important.

questions.question: What is the reason given for making prayer times specific instead of random?
questions.answer: The times match major changes in creation and signs of Allah’s care and gifts.

questions.question: What does the worshipper notice about creation before he bows?
questions.answer: He notices that all creation is under Allah’s command.

questions.question: Which parts of creation are mentioned to show this obedience?
questions.answer: Plants, animals, suns, and stars.

questions.question: What action follows saying “Allah is the Greatest” first in the passage?
questions.answer: Bowing.

questions.question: What action comes after thinking about the great submission of all creatures?
questions.answer: Prostration.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the end of created things in this world?
questions.answer: It describes them as leaving their duties in an organized way through death.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to some or all of them later?
questions.answer: They are raised back to life and prepared again for service.

questions.question: What natural event helps us understand this return to life?
questions.answer: The coming of spring.

questions.question: How is the human being described compared with the greatness of creation?
questions.answer: He is described as small and lowly, yet able to worship Allah.

questions.question: In what way does the person prostrate before Allah?
questions.answer: He prostrates with loving amazement, humility, and respectful self-lowering.

questions.question: What does this worship become for the believer?
questions.answer: It becomes a kind of spiritual journey upward.

questions.question: What does the passage say about performing ‘Isha in terms of feeling and meaning?
questions.answer: It is pleasant, elevated, meaningful, and serious.

questions.question: According to the final paragraph, what do the five prayer times point to?
questions.answer: They point to great changes, Allah’s mighty works, and His blessings for all.
